title: dsh source launch through the tsx ESM hook
summary: The dsh command is launched from TypeScript source through the tsx ESM hook, because Node 26 removed the flag the earlier launch method relied on.
firstReason: TypeScript tooling: a Go program is compiled, so there is no source-launch path, transformer hook or path mapping to choose.

title: One dsh launcher for application profiles
summary: Every application process starts through the one dsh command and a named profile (web, headless, sdk, sdk-minimal, acp); there are no separate application binaries with their own complete configuration.
firstReason: One launcher that owns composition, environment discovery and shutdown suits a single Go binary even better; keep it.

title: Config schema dump validation policy
summary: `dsh --dump-config-schema` projects plugin configuration declarations to JSON Schema without mounting plugins. The command exits 1 whenever any part of the projection is approximate, disabled rows are inspected too, and where native validation would change its input the schema is widened instead of simulating the change.
firstReason: A machine-readable configuration schema, and an exit code that says whether the document can replace native validation, are worth keeping. The approximations come from Schemastery's mutating validation and `!!js` expressions; Go configuration types can produce an exact schema, so the partial cases should disappear.

title: Generate the CLI reference from command help
summary: The command-line reference is generated by capturing the help text of the launcher, the plugin forwarder and every shipped profile, and following each listed subcommand, so it cannot omit a command or keep an old default.
firstReason: A reference generated from the real command tree is equally easy in Go and removes the same drift. The command-line area owns the generator.
